title: False fall: Bay County might feel a little cooler in the coming days. Here's the forecast - NewsBreak
text:
By Dylan Gentile ,
6 hours ago
PANAMA CITY — Fall isn't in the air, it's just an illusion, according to National Weather Service forecasters.
A cold front made its way into the region, leading to slightly below-average temperatures for this time of the year.
The NWS Tallahassee forecasting office expects average highs in the low 90s and average lows in the low 70s for late August. The meteorologists called the phenomenon a "fall preview."
While temperatures haven't declined dramatically, humidity is expected to fall. This will result in the temperatures not feeling as hot as they normally would.
Labor Day weekend is expected to be rainy in Panama City, with high daily chances for showers and thunderstorms. Labor Day itself features a 50% chance of showers and thunderstorms with partly sunny conditions expected.
"Locally heavy rainfall could lead to some localized flooding issues, with a marginal risk of excessive rainfall in place for Friday through Sunday," a meteorologist said in the local area forecast discussion.
While the weekend brings rain, it's also expected to bring a cool-off in temperatures. Highs through Labor Day weekend and into the next week are anticipated to be in the upper 80s, while lows sit around 70.
For those trying to hit the beach over the long weekend, the water is pretty warm. On Aug. 27, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration measured a temperature of 85 in both St Andrews Bay and Panama City Beach.
More on beaches: Fecal indicator bacteria prompt water quality advisories at five Bay County beaches
Yellow flags were flying over Panama City Beach on Aug. 27, indicating moderate surf or currents. Swimmers are advised to use caution. There was also a moderate rip current risk.
Looking ahead, the Climate Prediction Center is anticipating above-average temperatures and precipitation in our area over the next two weeks.
Meanwhile, the tropics are somewhat quiet. The only system being tracked by the National Hurricane Center is Tropical Storm Fernado, which is expected to head into the northern Atlantic Ocean without foreseeable landfall.
Although less-than-exciting for now, the CPC is tracking some potential tropical developments in the near future. Their global tropics hazard outlook depicts some low chances of cyclone formation in the central tropical Atlantic over the next two weeks.
Over the next three weeks, the chances of cyclone formation in that area increase to over 40%. This period also features a low chance of tropical development around the southern Gulf and to the south of the Yucatan Peninsula.
The NHC says that the peak of Hurricane Season is typically Sept. 10, with most activity between the mid-August and mid-October.
No severe weather activity is expected over the next three days, according to the Storm Prediction Center .
